stem: Where do you set the org's default language, locale, time zone and currency?
explanation: Company Information (Setup > Company Settings) holds the org defaults. Users can override locale, language and time zone for themselves.

stem: An admin enables multi-currency for Khanyisa Solar. What is true afterwards?

options.text: It can be turned off after 30 days
It can be turned off by a profile setting

explanation: Multi-currency is permanent once enabled. Person accounts are also permanent.

stem: Which setting determines which currency reports convert amounts into by default?
explanation: The corporate currency is the org's base currency. Other currencies convert to it using exchange rates.

stem: Which two settings does a support team use to define when it is open and when the escalation clock runs?
explanation: Business hours and holidays define working time, and escalation rules and entitlements can use them.

stem: A company's financial year starts in March and has four equal quarters. What should the admin configure?

options.text: A standard fiscal year starting in March
A custom fiscal year with its own period names
A business hours record that starts in March
A forecast category that shows the fiscal quarters

explanation: A standard fiscal year lets you pick the start month. A custom fiscal year is for unusual period patterns such as 4-4-5.

stem: What must be true about a Salesforce username?

options.text: It must be unique across all Salesforce orgs and look like an email address
It must match the user's real mailbox so they get emails
It must be unique only within your own org
It must be a phone number registered with the company

explanation: Usernames are globally unique and in email format, but do not have to be real mailboxes. The email field holds the real address.

stem: Which items are required when creating a user?

options.text: A role and a permission set
A profile and a permission set group

explanation: Every user needs a licence and one profile. Roles and permission sets are optional.

stem: An employee resigns. The admin needs to stop their login immediately but is not ready to free the licence. What should she do?
explanation: Freezing blocks login at once and keeps the licence. Deactivating blocks login and frees the licence. Users cannot be deleted.

stem: What happens to a user's licence when the user is deactivated?

options.text: It is freed for someone else
It is deleted from the org

explanation: Deactivated users do not use a licence. Frozen users do.

stem: Can an admin delete a user from Salesforce?

options.text: No, users can only be deactivated or frozen
Yes, from the Users page by an admin with the right permission
Yes, but only after the user has been inactive for 15 days
Yes, with a permission set that includes Delete Users

explanation: Users cannot be deleted. Deactivating preserves history such as record ownership.

objective: Explain licences, profiles, roles and permission sets
stem: Which of these controls visibility of other people's records up a management chain?
explanation: Roles form the hierarchy that can give managers access to records owned by their reports. Profiles control what a user can do.

objective: Explain licences, profiles, roles and permission sets
stem: Which of these decides which Salesforce features a user may use at all?
explanation: The licence sets the outer boundary of the features available. Profiles and permission sets work within it.

stem: Which sandbox type copies only configuration (metadata) and no real data?
explanation: Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes copy metadata only. Partial Copy adds a sample of data, Full copies all data.

stem: Which sandbox is best for final user acceptance testing with a complete copy of production data?
explanation: A Full sandbox copies metadata and all data, so testing reflects real volumes and values.

stem: A tester needs real-looking sample data but not the entire database. Which sandbox fits?
explanation: Partial Copy copies metadata plus a sample of data defined by a sandbox template.

stem: How far back does the Setup Audit Trail show changes in the Setup UI?
explanation: The Setup Audit Trail keeps 180 days. You can download it to review more history you have saved.

stem: An admin wants to know who changed a validation rule last month. Where should she look?
explanation: Setup Audit Trail records configuration changes: what changed, who changed it and when.

stem: What is delegated administration for?

options.text: Letting non-admins perform limited admin tasks, such as unlocking users
Giving one trusted user Modify All Data so that they can fix every problem
Sharing records with a manager so that they can see their team's work
Transferring record ownership when someone changes teams or leaves

explanation: Delegated administrators can do specific tasks for chosen roles or profiles without being full admins.

stem: What does My Domain provide?

options.text: A custom address for your org, needed for features such as single sign-on
A sandbox that copies all of your production metadata and some data
A backup of your data that can be restored on demand by an admin
A custom object that stores your company's addresses for records

explanation: My Domain gives your org its own subdomain and is required for many features, including SSO.

stem: Which TWO of these are permanent once enabled in an org? (Choose 2)
explanation: Both multi-currency and person accounts cannot be disabled once on. Business hours and sandboxes can be changed or removed.

stem: A user wants dates shown in their own time zone, different from the org default. What should happen?

options.text: The user changes their own time zone in their settings
The admin changes the org's default time zone for everyone
A new profile is created with the other time zone
A new sandbox is created with the other time zone

explanation: Locale, language and time zone can be set per user and override the org default.

stem: Before deactivating a user who owns many records and approvals, what should the admin do?

options.text: Reassign what they own and remove them from processes that depend on them
Delete all of their records first, so that nothing is left owned by an inactive user
Freeze everyone in their role until the reassignment has been completed
Change their username so that they cannot log in while you finish

explanation: Reassigning ownership, approvals, queue membership and rule references prevents broken processes.

stem: A sales rep has left Khanyisa Solar. She owns 120 open leads and is named as the default owner in a lead assignment rule. What is the correct order of actions?

options.text: Reassign her records, update the rule, then deactivate the user
Delete the user first, and then reassign her records to a new owner
Freeze the user permanently and leave the assignment rule as it is
Change her profile to Chatter Free so that she cannot own records

explanation: Users cannot be deleted, and deactivating is blocked while automation still names the user. Clean up first, then deactivate to free the licence.

stem: The admin must stop a user from logging in immediately while a manager decides what to do with their records. The licence should stay assigned for now. Which action fits?
explanation: Freezing blocks login at once without freeing the licence. Deactivation frees it and needs the cleanup first.

stem: A team must test a major release against a copy of production data volume before go-live. Which sandbox fits best?
explanation: A Full sandbox copies all metadata and data, so it suits performance and volume testing.
